The purpose of this survey was to understand the influence of adaptive lighting on perceptions of safety, security, and energy efficiency from the standpoint of the general population in a city or town. The survey data will help identify perceptions and potential strategies to implement adaptive lighting. Representatives of public organizations were emailed a link to an online survey, and were asked to distribute the link to their members or other residents that may be interested. A different survey was administered depending on whether the targeted area used adaptive lighting or not. The survey was released online from March 12, 2021, to June 30, 2021. The survey began with an introduction describing the goal of the project and the goals of the survey. Participation in the survey was entirely voluntary, and the participants’ privacy was protected. The survey was approved by the Virginia Tech Institutional Review Board. The survey had a list of 21 multiple-choice questions for the cities with adaptive lighting and a list of 15 questions to cities without adaptive lighting. 4.2 Results The results from the analysis are shown first for crashes, then crime and finally the focus groups and the surveys. 4.2.1 Crash Analysis During this data analysis, the project team analyzed 2010–2019 crash data for Cambridge and Somerville in detail in an effort to understand if the ALS had safety effects. Based on data availability, the project team used the following variables in the analysis: • Adaptive lighting indicator. This is a binary variable indicating if the lighting system is adaptive. It also serves as the indicator for the two cities, with 1 indicating Cambridge and 0 indicating Somerville. • Year index. During this analysis, the project team obtained yearly annual average daily traffic (AADT) information based on the state HPMS yearly submittals to FHWA. The data contained in the HPMS datasets are yearly snapshots of the AADT information maintained by MassDOT. Note that it is common practice that state DOTs update AADT for major on-system roadways more frequently than minor roadways. Due to this reason, many minor HPMS segments contained the 51 same AADT values spanning multiple years, possibly due to either not being updated or non-changing AADT values. The year index variable is a continuous whole number between 1 and 10, with 1 indicating the year 2010 and 10 indicating the year 2019. The use of the year index variable was intended to capture AADT changes over the analysis period that were not reflected in the actual AADT values. • Roadway variables.
